key_insight: A generalized mean-field bond model predicts finite-temperature thermodynamics of multispecies, multisublattice crystals without statistical sampling.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a route to thermodynamic predictions for complex crystalline materials without sampling-intensive molecular dynamics.
method: Represent each Wyckoff position by one atom and solve reference-bond densities for its neighbor shells.
Use zero-temperature force constants to construct bond–bond correlations.
Enforce a common virial temperature and compatibility between average bond lengths and crystal volume.
evidence_signal: For unary, binary, and ternary crystals with shell-specific Morse-type potentials, predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with molecular dynamics within statistical uncertainty.
watch_item: Ab initio accuracy remains a proposed extension; validation here uses Morse-type potentials parametrized from empirical-potential force constants.
paper_title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
